title: Manifest dispatch worker with shutdown hook
name: Manifest dispatch worker

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles graceful shutdown? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
In ShutdownCoordinator.run, why set health.ready = false and then sleep for loadBalancerDelayMs before doing anything else?
choices: To give the carrier gateway time to finish its HTTP calls.
To make the readiness probe fail so the load balancer stops routing new traffic here, and to wait long enough for it to notice.
To let Hikari return all connections to the pool before it is closed.
Because Runtime shutdown hooks must run at least one second before the JVM halts.

questions.prompt: In ManifestWorker.process, the catch block for CancellationException rethrows before the generic catch (e: Exception). What is the effect?
choices: Cancelled jobs are retried automatically by the channel.
The exception is logged twice, once per catch block.
Cancellation would be recorded as a carrier failure in the database if the rethrow were not there, and the coroutine would not actually stop.
When the scope is cancelled, the job is not marked FAILED and the cancellation propagates so the coroutine really ends; the generic handler only sees genuine errors.

questions.prompt: drain() calls inbox.close() and then waits on consumers.joinAll(). What happens to manifests already buffered in the channel when close() is called?
choices: Consumers still receive everything already buffered, then their for-loops end, so joinAll completes once the backlog is processed.
They are discarded immediately and consumers exit.
close() suspends until the buffer is empty.
Consumers keep waiting indefinitely because close() only affects blocked senders.
